intro: One research run each weekday morning (about 07:00 Berlin). Monday's edition also covers Saturday and Sunday. Up to about 10 items, chosen by relevance rather than to fill a quota. Official sources are checked every day; news outlets and web search fill in the rest. Paywalled outlets only contribute headlines.
rules: Plain language throughout: short sentences, everyday words, abbreviations spelled out the first time, and technical terms either explained in a few words or replaced (for example 'put into national law' instead of 'transpose').

Heat gets priority: anything on heatwaves, urban heat, heat-health, cooling or heat adaptation is ranked one level higher than it would otherwise be, is never dropped to stay within 10 items, and carries a Heat tag.

High: EU or national laws and policies reaching a milestone (proposals, deals, votes, final adoption, guidance), consultations with a deadline, major science or monitoring reports, results of UN climate talks, funding calls for cities or local governments opening or closing soon.
Notable: important studies, developments in markets, grids or prices, adaptation practice and climate impacts in Europe, events worth attending.
Dropped: routine press releases, opinion pieces with no new facts, company news with no policy relevance, and repeats of stories from the last 7 days unless something new happened.
Global climate science stays in. Policy, calls and impacts focus on Europe and European cities.
Energy poverty and energy communities appear under Cities & local government or Energy systems where they fit.
One Top story per edition. Every item gets a 'For cities' line, a link to the source and, where one exists, a link to the full text (report, legal text or call document).
Relevance first: a quiet day gets fewer items, never filler.
